description: A Road-Flooding Fix for a California State Park is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by California Department of Parks and Recreation; Marin County Board of Supervisors; Marin County Department of Public Works. Flooding from rain and extreme high tides often leaves the road to San Francisco's China Camp State Park inaccessible. So a diverse group of stakeholders, with support from NOAA’s Science Collaborative team, proposed raising the road. Coverage: California (2021). The toolkit gives California as the location, 2021 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
